title: The Table Is the Point
excerpt: On why we called this kitchen Breaking Bread, and why the best meals are measured in conversations, not compliments.

body.text: Breaking bread is one of the oldest ideas we have. To share a loaf with someone is to make room for them: at your table, in your day, in your life. That is why we chose the name.

It carries a quieter meaning for us too. The phrase runs through the Christian story of fellowship and gratitude, of people gathered around a simple meal and finding something bigger there. That spirit, of thankfulness and an open table, sits gently underneath everything we cook.

Most of the recipes here are built to be shared. Big trays, slow braises, a lasagne that feeds eight, a loaf you tear rather than slice. Not because cooking for one doesn't matter, but because food tastes better with company.
The best meals are measured in conversations, not compliments.
So cook something generous. Invite someone you haven't seen in a while. Put the pan in the middle of the table and let everyone help themselves. That's the whole idea.
